records.notes: kb/Work PB284: PROSE-PARAGRAPH row. §9.1.16 paragraph 4: while locked by a file connector a record is not accessible to another connector of the same or another run unit except by READ with IGNORING LOCK; the holding connector may re-access it. Read: FileRegistry.ConflictOnLockedRecord is the one access check, asked by both governed READ entries (ReadShared, ReadKeyedShared), RewriteShared and DeleteShared before anything is committed; it asks PhysicalFileTable.HolderOf, which answers None for the asking connector's own lock (the holder re-accesses) and names a holder in this or another run unit otherwise, and the access then ends RecordLocked ('51') through the RETRY rules (GR-9.1.13.8-1, GR-14.9.30.4-9); its first statement returns no conflict for IGNORING LOCK, the one place GR-14.9.30.4-12 is applied. PhysicalFileTable.LockRecord refuses another connector's grant with '51' and is idempotent for the holder (GR-12.4.5.9.4-8), all CONFORMS. || editions 2002,2014,2023 (kb/Work PB284): record locking and the sharing/locking I-O statuses are decided at 2002 for the sibling rows GR-9.1.15-1..3, GR-9.1.13.8-1 and GR-9.1.13.9-1 (kb/Work PB3173), and this paragraph states the same facility.
records.retire-reason: ReadLockGovern, the post-read Format-2 patch, was replaced by ReadKeyedShared (kb/Work PB338); FileRegistry.cs names it only in a comment, and the paragraph's access check is ConflictOnLockedRecord
